name: Omar Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach beginner guitar on Mondays, play the Thursday hotel lounge and record simple parts for local singers when asked. I finished secondary school and still work at making six children listen to me at once.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What matters to you, and what is hardest?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like a beginner finding the right chord without me moving their hand. The hardest part is not knowing whether the hotel will keep the same Thursdays next quarter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the hotel lounge manager that an easier booking sheet is welcome, but the guests still ask for live guitar on Thursdays. I would keep the same set unless the manager asks us to change it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have three months of expenses saved and my partner’s clinic receptionist pay arrives regularly. One poor lounge night would not threaten the mortgage, though a whole season of lost dates would.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep my Thursday lounge set and Monday beginner guitar pupils this season. I would ask the manager for the next quarter’s dates before making summer plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the hotel schedule, but household pay is steady right now. The AI story does not change the mortgage date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened on the last quiet lounge night?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The last quiet Thursday still paid the written fee. I would rather keep that agreement than argue about whether an app can choose a set list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does your daughter say about your paper notes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My daughter asks why I still write chord changes by hand. I remember chord changes better when I write them by hand. She is free to learn differently.

say: I would tell the manager that **live Thursday guitar** still matters to guests.
I would keep the **written lounge fee** for quiet nights.
think: Our **three-month cushion** and partner’s clinic pay cover one poor night.
A whole lost **hotel season** could still disturb the mortgage.
do: Keep **Thursday lounge sets** and Monday guitar pupils this season.
Ask the manager for **next-quarter dates** before summer plans.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about hotel dates while household pay remains steady.
S0.quote: I remember chord changes better when I write them by hand.
fieldNote: His **moderate cushion** and regular partner income support an uneasy rather than anxious baseline.
He uses **paper notes** and avoids AI tools, consistent with his resistant profile.

steps.text: Keep Thursday hotel guitar sets and Monday beginner pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the hotel may use AI to book, advertise and choose background music, but it should tell us before reducing live dates. I would ask the manager for a written quarter of paid sets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The simple recording parts I make for local singers might lose buyers. A smaller lounge schedule is possible too. Three months saved would give us time, not make the lost pay harmless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask for the hotel’s paid-date list and my last three invoices. If the manager cuts dates in the first year, I would ask the community school for a paid beginner group only if staff stay in the room, preparation is paid and the time fits child pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious because my own recording pay could shrink and lounge dates might follow. I am not sure either will happen at once.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you teach six children tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can teach one child at a time, but a group of six is beyond me now. I would ask the school tutor to observe me first if that hour is paid. I would take six pupils only if the tutor says I am ready.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would collect your children during that class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner’s clinic shift ends at four on some days. We would agree the pickup day before I promise a school class.

say: I would ask for a **written quarter** of paid hotel sets.
I would tell management to discuss **live date cuts** before changing the schedule.
think: My **recording parts** could lose buyers as AI makes music cheaply.
A smaller **hotel schedule** would reduce household pay despite three months saved.
do: Request the **hotel date list** and three recent invoices next month.
Seek a **paid school group** if hotel dates fall, only after funded observation and tutor approval, with staff, preparation pay and pickup.
Observe the **school tutor** before a larger class only if the observation hour is paid.
feel: I feel **anxious** about realistic fee loss, though the cushion gives time.
S1.quote: Three months saved would give us time, not make the lost pay harmless.
fieldNote: He names **recording income** as the first likely thinking-AI loss, while a smaller hotel schedule remains possible.
The school group requires **paid observation and preparation**, staff presence and reliable pickup.

steps.text: Keep Monday guitar pupils while hotel dates are checked
Observe school tutor if the observation hour is paid
Ask school for paid group if hotel dates fall, paid observation and tutor approval complete
Confirm staff, preparation pay and child pickup before taking school group

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the hotel that AGI by 2028 could choose tracks and answer guests, but a live player still needs a fee. I would ask for a decision on our Thursday run before the next quarter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the recording parts to vanish in 2028 and the manager may cut some lounge dates. Robots for hands-on performance arrive around 2031. A playlist could replace me sooner than a robot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask for the written Thursday schedule and check whether two nearby schools have open classroom aide posts that accept secondary school education. If 2028 AGI cuts the lounge dates, I would apply for a suitable open post only if the hours fit pickup, and use savings above two months for the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about losing my own recording fees and possible hotel nights, but I can pay the mortgage for a few months. I would not leave teaching for a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you stop giving guitar lessons?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school aide post has to be real and paid. I would keep Monday pupils until a written offer arrives, even if an interview goes well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your partner about the cushion?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner we can cover the mortgage during a search, but not forever. I would ask the hotel for a date, not tell our children we are moving tomorrow.

say: I would ask for a **Thursday schedule** before the next hotel quarter.
I would say **live guitar** deserves a fee even with cheap tracks.
think: My **recording parts** likely vanish in 2028 before 2031 stage robots.
The hotel could cut **live dates** before a robot plays guitar.
do: Ask the hotel for a **written schedule** this week.
Apply for an **open school aide post** after 2028 cuts only if qualified and pickup fits.
Use savings **above two months** for a search if hotel dates fall.
feel: I feel **anxious** about lost fees, with enough savings for a short search.
S2.quote: A playlist could replace me sooner than a robot.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **2028 desk-work loss** from later 2031 hands-on robot capability.
His fallback needs **real paid vacancies** and suitable education and pickup, with guitar lessons kept until an offer.

steps.text: Apply for open aide post if hotel dates fall, qualifications and pickup fit
Keep Monday guitar pupils until a written school offer arrives

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the hotel that AGI by 2031 gives us several seasons to agree what a live lounge set earns. I would ask for a contract that states the minimum number of Thursdays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think recording parts end by 2031, but I could improve my group teaching before then. Robots around 2034 might play onstage, although I do not know whether hotel guests would stay for that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This autumn I would ask the community school to fund two observations of a senior guitar teacher, with pickup covered at home. If the tutor approves me for a paid group, I would take it; in the first year after 2031 I would keep the group only with school staff present, paid preparation and a written term of pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious until the school work is real. The five years help me practise, but the recording fees still have to be replaced.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take six beginners before an observation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am not ready to manage six beginners by myself. I would not promise a six-child guitar group until a school tutor has watched me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can the clinic schedule cover that class each week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I could swap pickup on her early clinic days. If the school needs every Thursday, that will not work with the lounge set, so I would ask for another day.

say: I would ask for a **minimum paid Thursday count** in the hotel contract.
I would seek **funded observation** before a school group.
think: My **recording income** may end by 2031 before 2034 stage robots.
A **paid school group** could replace some fees if I qualify.
do: Request two **funded tutor observations** this autumn with pickup arranged.
Keep a **paid school group** after 2031 only with approval, staff, preparation pay, enrolled pupils and workable pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** until group pay replaces recording fees.
S3.quote: I would not promise a six-child guitar group until a school tutor has watched me.
fieldNote: He asks for **paid supervised learning** before taking six beginners.
The paid class requires **staff and preparation pay**, plus a workable day, not merely a school room.

steps.text: Observe senior guitar teacher twice if school funds it and pickup works
Keep paid group after 2031 only if approved, staffed and preparation is paid
Confirm written term enrollment and workable pickup before keeping the school group

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that AGI by 2036 leaves time to learn music and another useful skill. I would keep playing hotel sets while the manager pays a written live fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 I might teach a paid group that replaces recording money. Robots around 2039 may take some live sets, but my partner and I can plan with our current three months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would put part of each paid hotel fee into savings after the mortgage and food clear. In the first year after 2036 I would compare actual hotel and school pay, and apply for a qualified open school aide role if both incomes fall short and pickup works.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be uneasy about the distant stage question. The next few years of current work feel manageable with the cushion we have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What money would you actually save?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would save only from a paid set, not from a date the manager mentions. If hotel nights fall early, I would keep two months of expenses for the mortgage while I search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach your children about work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that learning a trade and keeping a promise matter. Playing music is honest work when someone pays for it.

say: I would tell my children to **learn useful work** and keep promises.
I would keep playing **paid hotel sets** under written terms.
think: A paid **school group** could replace recording money before 2036.
Possible **2039 robots** could change hotel work, but current pay is stable.
do: Save part of each **paid hotel fee** after mortgage and food this year.
Apply for a **qualified school aide role** after 2036 only if both incomes fall short and pickup fits.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant changes while current work and savings hold.
S4.quote: Playing music is honest work when someone pays for it.
fieldNote: His savings rule counts **paid hotel fees** after essential bills, with a two-month floor.
A later school move still needs **qualification and pickup fit**, plus a real opening.

steps.text: Save part of paid hotel fees after mortgage and food while keeping two months untouched
Apply for qualified open school aide role if 2036 incomes fall short and pickup fits
Keep hotel sets while manager pays written live fee

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because recording parts may go before the hotel confirms its live dates. Written Thursdays, a paid teaching route and an open school post I qualify for would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the hotel who stays to hear a live guitar after dinner. A quiet room can still hold people who came for the music.

headlineQuote: A quiet room can still hold people who came for the music.
portrait: At **43**, Omar is a junior guitarist with secondary school education, two children, a mortgage and three months saved.
His partner’s **clinic pay** steadies the household, but hotel and recording dates remain uncertain.
He avoids **AI tools** and seeks paid tutor observation before managing a larger school class.
Across AGI dates, he protects **written hotel fees** and considers qualified school work only with real openings and pickup fit.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** may erase recording parts before the hotel confirms paid live dates.
whatWouldHelp: **Written hotel dates**, paid teaching preparation and a qualified school opening would help Omar plan.
